chapter_name: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the touching story of a young girl teaching her grandmother to read, proving that there is absolutely no age limit for learning!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The grandmother loved the popular Kannada novel 'Kashi Yatre' published weekly in a magazine. Since she was illiterate, her 12-year-old granddaughter (the author) used to read it to her.

Once, the granddaughter went away for a wedding. The grandmother received the magazine but felt completely helpless because she couldn't read a single word. She cried, realizing the pain of dependency.
The grandmother requested her young granddaughter to become her teacher. She set a strict deadline (Saraswati Pooja festival) to learn the Kannada alphabet so she could read independently.

With immense hard work and determination, the grandmother learned to read perfectly. On Saraswati Pooja, she touched her granddaughter's feet as a mark of respect for her 'teacher', showing that respect is for knowledge, not just age.

fun_activity.title: 👵 Teacher for a Day
fun_activity.instructions: Ask your grandparents or an older person in your family if there is any new technology (like using a smartphone app or sending a voice note) they want to learn. Teach it to them patiently, just like the girl in the story!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the name of the novel ('Kashi Yatre') and why the grandmother related to its main character (an old lady wanting to visit Kashi).
📌 Understand the cultural significance of the grandmother touching the granddaughter's feet—it was a tribute to a teacher, breaking the tradition of age.
📌 Write about how education brings independence and self-respect.
quick_recap: ⭐ The author of this beautiful autobiographical story is Sudha Murty.
⭐ The grandmother proved that if you are determined, you can overcome any obstacle, even old age.
⭐ The grandmother gifted her teacher (the granddaughter) a dress material as a token of gratitude.
